title: Auth/audit incident follow-up: SLO recalibration, alert noise reduction, and admin playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Follow-up work after March 2026 auth/audit degradation that caused delayed admin session audit events and noisy alerts. This ticket captures measurable SLO changes, alert tuning, audit pipeline fixes, a dedicated admin-controls playbook, and validation plans for RBAC v2 + SSO/SAML interactions.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed sustained increases in auth event processing latency and a spike of 'audit_ingest_backlog' alerts. Impact: delayed audit events for admin actions (5-15 minute ingestion lag), triggering downstream reconciliation failures and noisy on-call alerts. Root causes identified: 1) audit pipeline shard imbalance after a config rollout, 2) RBAC v2 migration created higher-cardinality admin events that were not covered by existing sampling and routing rules, 3) an overly-sensitive alert that fired on transient backlog spikes.
postmortem_summary: Contributing factors were a config rollout for audit sharding (misaligned routing keys) and RBAC v2 increasing cardinality of admin_identity fields. The audit producer and consumer both recovered, but gaps in SLO definitions and alert thresholds caused noisy paging. We accepted operational risk during rollout without sufficient synthetic traffic validation and missed a monitoring gap for admin-level event latency.
updates: 2026-03-10: Triage meeting - agreed scope: fix ingestion routing, revise SLOs for admin audit latency, tune alerts, add synthetic monitoring, and publish an admin incident playbook.
2026-03-11: Investigated shard config drift; confirmed a bad regex used in routing table for 'admin' namespace. Patch drafted. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3421
2026-03-11: Short-term mitigation deployed: increased consumer parallelism and temporarily bumped audit pipeline retry budget to drain backlog (ops runbook invoked).

2026-03-12: Alert tuning proposal posted in #security-observability for review - reduce flapping by adding a 3m sustained-window and ignoring <50 events/minute transient spikes. Link to proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUTH/Alert+Tuning+Proposal

2026-03-13: SLO recalibration draft: split audit SLOs into two classes - admin-critical (99th pct processing latency target 30s) and bulk-event (95th pct target 2m). Rationale: admin actions must be near-real-time for compliance + incident response; bulk events have different economics.
2026-03-13: PR merged to fix routing regex and add additional routing unit tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/1a2b3c4d

2026-03-14: Created synthetic traffic job (k8s cron) to exercise admin event path under RBAC v2 cardinality. Job in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-tools/blob/main/synthetics/admin-load.yaml
2026-03-14: On-call debrief recorded; agreed to ship playbook and monitoring within the week and to quarantine alerting changes behind a feature flag for gradual rollout.
decision_log: Decision 1 (2026-03-10): Prioritize admin-audit latency SLOs over bulk-event cost optimizations. Owner: Priya Shah.
Decision 2 (2026-03-11): Fix routing regex in infra and add a CI check to prevent future shard key regressions. Owner: Linus Carter.
Decision 3 (2026-03-12): Alert window change to 3m sustained with explanatory annotations in alert messages; avoid paging for short-lived backlogs <50 events/min. Owner: Marco Nguyen.
Decision 4 (2026-03-13): Introduce synthetic admin traffic in CI to validate RBAC v2 changes pre-rollout. Owner: Aisha Patel.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increasing consumer parallelism temporarily reduces backlog risk but increases short-term cost and might mask upstream producer problems.
Stricter admin SLOs (30s p99) require more aggressive resource allocation or smarter batching, which has cost implications for hosted customers; tradeoff accepted for security/compliance workloads.
Raising alert thresholds reduces noise but may delay detection of some real regressions; mitigated by synthetic checks and richer alert context.
action_items: A1: Deploy routing regex fix + add unit tests. Owner: Linus Carter. ETA: 2026-03-12 (done).
A2: Formalize SLO split: define SLOs, error budget policy, and rollback thresholds. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-18.
A3: Implement alert tuning behind feature flag and run canary for 72h. Owner: Marco Nguyen. ETA: 2026-03-16.
A4: Add synthetic admin traffic job to CI and dashboard. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-03-14 (in prod).
A5: Update on-call runbooks with a specific checklist for audit_ingest_backlog incidents and RBAC v2 related failures. Owner: Jordan Lee. ETA: 2026-03-17.
A6: Create compliance-facing summary and retention proof of admin audit events for legal ops. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-21.
A7: Postmortem doc & playbook published to Confluence and linked in the alert message. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2026-03-15.
runbook_updates: Added step: check routing table regex and shard counts (commands provided) - new section 'Audit shard health'.
Added step: run synthetic admin traffic validation via 'auth-tools admin-check' before any RBAC v2 rollout.
Added step: escalation matrix when p99 admin latency > 60s for > 5 minutes (pager + exec notification).
qa_checklist: Synthetic admin events show p99 < 30s for three consecutive runs.
Alert feature flag toggled in canary for 72h with no missed real incidents in that window.
Unit tests cover routing regex variations and high-cardinality identity values.
End-to-end test validates audit event appears in GCS/log-store with expected admin_identity field within SLO window.
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/auth-audit-slo (added new panels for admin p50/p95/p99).
Metric: audit_ingest_backlog_count (alert threshold revised: sustained > 300 for 3m -> page only if > 500 for 5m).
notes_for_pm_and_design_review: PM: Ensure the admin SLOs are reflected in SLAs for Dedicated and Private customers who require audit timeliness. Owner: Priya Shah.
Design: We should add contextual links in the console alert UI to the playbook and recent incident timeline to reduce cognitive load during paging. Owner: Maya Gomez. ETA: 2026-03-20.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Admin p99 audit processing latency <= 30s in synthetics for 24h running window.
2) On-call alerts for audit_ingest_backlog reduced by >80% compared to pre-change noise for 7 days.
3) Playbook published and linked in alert messages and console, with runbook steps validated in two drills.
4) CI gates include synthetic admin run for RBAC v2 PRs.
